"""Build the Applied Performance Annual Report 2025-2026 (Executive).

Run:  python build_annual_report_2025_2026.py [--pdf]

Writes YYYY-MM-DD_Applied_Annual_Report_2025_2026_Executive.docx (and .pdf with
--pdf, exported through Word) into the DEPARTMENT_ANNUAL_REPORT folder. Every
number below is traced in the companion ..._SOURCES.md. To re-label an item after
it ships, change its status text here and rebuild; do not hand-edit the .docx.
"""
import datetime
import os
import sys

DEV = os.path.expanduser("~/Desktop/DEV")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(DEV, "Baylor_Doc_Style"))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(DEV, "Tech_Inventory_Analysis", "scripts"))
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc  # noqa: E402

OUT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
TODAY = datetime.date.today().isoformat()
STEM = "{}_Applied_Annual_Report_2025_2026_Executive".format(TODAY)

d = BaylorDoc(
    "Applied Performance Annual Report 2025-2026",
    deck="A foundation year: the data and education infrastructure the department will run on.",
    status="Draft for review",
    eyebrow="BAYLOR ATHLETICS · HEALTH AND WELLNESS",
)
d.meta([
    ["Prepared by", "Eric Rash, Director of Applied Performance"],
    ["Prepared for", "Kenny Boyd"],
    ["Reporting period", "October 2025 to September 2026"],
    ["Status", "Draft for review, October 2026"],
])
d.callout(
    "How to read the status labels",
    "**Delivered** means the work reached a person or team, with a dated record. "
    "**Built** means the work is complete and has a scheduled launch. "
    "**In development** means work is under way. **Deferred** means it moved to 2026/27.",
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Executive summary
d.section("Executive Summary")
d.subhead("Department Mission Statement")
d.para("Drive the elite performance of championship-level athletic programs by leveraging "
       "science and technology through education and relationships.")

d.subhead("The year in one line")
d.para("2025/26 was a foundation year. With one fewer staff member for half of it, the "
       "department built the data stores and the education library it will deliver from in "
       "2026/27, and put both to work with Volleyball and the HHPR graduate program.")

d.subhead("Key Achievements 2025/2026")
d.numbered([
    "**Centralized, queryable athlete data.** Football GPS and force plate testing moved from "
    "spreadsheet files into central databases that update twice a day without manual entry. "
    "Across the year they hold 11,289 force plate tests from 507 athletes in 15 sports and "
    "10,390 football GPS athlete-sessions. The department also ran Athletics' first "
    "department-wide technology inventory: 32 of 32 units, 188 products, delivered to Kenny "
    "Boyd on October 1.",
    "**Kinexon expanded to Volleyball.** Following Women's Basketball (2024), Volleyball now has "
    "a Kinexon database, a dashboard and a post-practice report. Wenger and Ryan McGuyre use it "
    "every week; the fall camp block alone covered 6 practices, 16 athletes and 8,870 "
    "measurements.",
    "**An education library, built and scheduled.** Eric taught the graduate course HHPR 5355 "
    "in Spring 2026 with Chris Ruf and Wenger. The department also built 49 finished education "
    "pieces: 45 TeamTalk short talks, two Research in 5 paper reviews and the first two "
    "lessons of a return-to-play course for Athletic Medicine. Each has a launch quarter and "
    "an audience in Section 4.",
])

d.subhead("Strategic Vision")
d.para("Applied Performance continues as a project-based group without sport assignments, "
       "serving three areas: student-athlete and staff education; performance data, analytics "
       "and planning; and research and development. This year the department added the "
       "infrastructure underneath all three: shared data stores, a technology inventory, and a "
       "library of education material ready to deliver.")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Section 1
d.section("Year in Review")
d.subhead("1.1  2025/26 Goal Scorecard")
d.para("Each Key Result Indicator from last year's report, with its status and the evidence "
       "behind it.")
d.table(
    ["2025/26 Key Result Indicator", "Status", "Evidence"],
    [
        ["**Goal 1 — Education**", "", ""],
        ["Launch four Performance School modules (Technologies, Planning & Monitoring, Load "
         "Prescription, Return to Play)", "Built",
         "Plan, curriculum map and session outlines complete (Dec 2025); TeamTalk decks cover "
         "all four topics. Launch Q2-Q3 2026/27."],
        ["Develop three Performance Academy topics (Sleep, Travel, Recovery)", "Built",
         "TeamTalk decks on sleep debt, sleep tracking, travel nutrition, active recovery and "
         "cold exposure. Launch Q2 2026/27."],
        ["Athletics staff teach in the academic program (HHPR 5355)", "Delivered",
         "Taught Spring 2026 with Chris Ruf and Wenger."],
        ["**Goal 2 — Data and analytics**", "", ""],
        ["Centralized data storage with secure access for three user groups", "In development",
         "GPS, force plate and Kinexon Volleyball stores built. Volleyball staff have access "
         "through the dashboard and a shared workbook; access for the other two groups is "
         "scheduled for Q3."],
        ["Migrate more than 50% of data from Excel to a database", "Built",
         "GPS, force plate and Kinexon Volleyball data now live in databases. The share of all "
         "department data is not tracked."],
        ["Evaluate and cost at least two analytics platforms", "In development",
         "Databricks demonstration held October 5. A cost review of 184 products with the "
         "Business Office (Erin Boyette) began October 1."],
        ["**Goal 3 — Research**", "", ""],
        ["Develop three research questions with HHPR", "Delivered",
         "Cold-room recovery, DEXA body composition and a force plate injury study were scoped "
         "with Dr. Andrew Gallucci (Nov-Dec 2025); the steering committee approved the injury "
         "study in January."],
        ["Co-author one research paper with HHPR", "Delivered",
         "Soccer body composition paper, J Strength Cond Res, December 2025."],
        ["Put one research finding into a training protocol", "Deferred",
         "Paused after the staff departure; carried into 2026/27 (Q4)."],
        ["Establish a research review group (Think Tank)", "Delivered",
         "Athletics research steering committee approved its first project January 30, 2026."],
        ["Build a research database", "In development",
         "Project catalog started; restart planned for Q2 2026/27."],
    ],
    widths=[2.6, 0.95, 3.15],
)

d.subhead("1.2  Quantitative Impact")
d.para("The first four rows repeat last year's measures. Those counts were not kept in a "
       "store this year, so they are marked not tracked rather than estimated. The rows below "
       "them are counted directly from the department's databases and records.")
d.table(
    ["Metric", "2023/24", "2024/25", "2025/26", "How it was counted"],
    [
        ["Performance Assessments", "5", "7", "Not tracked", "No count kept this year"],
        ["Load Management Reports", "50+", "100+", "Not tracked", "No count kept this year"],
        ["Technology Touchpoints", "500+", "800+", "Not tracked",
         "Replaced by the measured rows below"],
        ["Research Projects", "8", "10", "6", "Named projects in research meeting notes"],
        ["Force plate tests stored", "—", "—", "11,289",
         "Tests dated Oct 2025-Sep 2026; 507 athletes, 15 sports"],
        ["Football GPS athlete-sessions", "—", "—", "10,390",
         "124 sessions, 144 athletes, Oct 2025-Sep 2026"],
        ["Volleyball Kinexon measurements", "—", "—", "8,870",
         "Fall camp: 6 practices, 16 athletes, 68 metrics"],
        ["Volleyball load workbook rows", "—", "—", "7,384", "Shared workbook, October 2"],
        ["Units inventoried", "—", "—", "32 of 32", "52 survey responses"],
        ["Technology products catalogued", "—", "—", "188",
         "75 hold athlete data; 9 retired"],
        ["Education pieces built", "—", "—", "49",
         "45 TeamTalk + 2 Research in 5 + 2 course lessons"],
        ["Education deliveries (dated)", "—", "—", "6", "Listed in 1.3, Case Study 3"],
    ],
    widths=[1.75, 0.6, 0.6, 0.85, 2.9],
    numeric_cols=(1, 2, 3),
    caption="Database counts taken October 6, 2026 from the GPS, force plate and Kinexon "
            "stores. Force plate counts leave out staff and archived profiles.",
)

d.subhead("1.3  Success Stories & Case Studies")
d.para("**Case Study 1: Volleyball load monitoring with Kinexon**", space_after=2)
d.para("**Sport:** Volleyball (Wenger, Ryan McGuyre).")
d.para("**Challenge:** Volleyball had wearable data but no consistent way to turn a practice "
       "into a coach-ready summary the next morning.")
d.para("**Intervention:** Built a Kinexon database for Volleyball, a dashboard and a one-page "
       "post-practice report that draw from the same numbers, so the two always agree. A shared "
       "load workbook (7,384 rows) gives staff the season view.")
d.para("**Outcome:** Wenger and Ryan McGuyre used the dashboard every week through the summer "
       "block. Fall camp (6 practices, 16 athletes, 8,870 measurements) showed one skills "
       "session carrying almost twice the jumps of any other, which is the kind of finding the "
       "staff can now plan around. Exporting every practice at drill level is the next step.")

d.para("**Case Study 2: Department-wide Technology Inventory**", space_after=2)
d.para("**Scope:** All of Athletics (requested by Kenny Boyd).")
d.para("**Challenge:** Athletics needed one view of what technology each unit runs, who "
       "pays for it and which products hold athlete data, ahead of the FY28 budget cycle.")
d.para("**Intervention:** Ran a department-wide survey, matched answers to Business Office "
       "records, and produced a summary, findings, product lists and a by-unit list in the "
       "house style.")
d.para("**Outcome:** 52 responses covering 32 of 32 units, 188 products, 75 that hold athlete "
       "data and 9 marked for retirement. Delivered to Kenny Boyd on October 1. It now feeds "
       "the cost and use-agreement review with Erin Boyette and the Executive Team summary due "
       "before November 30.")

d.para("**Case Study 3: Education for Athletic Medicine and staff**", space_after=2)
d.para("**Audience:** Athletic Medicine (Joe Smith), Athletic Performance staff, HHPR.")
d.para("**Challenge:** Return-to-play decisions sit between Athletic Medicine and Athletic "
       "Performance, and staff asked for shared, practical material.")
d.para("**Intervention:** A joint return-to-play talk with Jeremy (July 8; 17 slides and a "
       "workbook), followed by a constraints-based return-to-play course for Joe Smith: two of "
       "eight lessons built, each with a one-page cheat sheet.")
d.para("**Outcome:** Six dated education deliveries this year: HHPR 5355 (Spring 2026); the "
       "Acrobatics & Tumbling training-plan presentation to HHPR (February 19); the return-to-play "
       "talk (July 8); the Shiftwave staff deck (August 3); the course package to Joe Smith "
       "(October 6); and Research in 5 #001 to Athletic Performance staff (October 6).")

d.subhead("1.4  Technology & Innovation Implementations")
d.table(
    ["Technology", "Sport / unit", "Status", "What it does"],
    [
        ["Kinexon (expansion)", "Volleyball", "Delivered",
         "Database, dashboard and post-practice report in weekly use"],
        ["Central data stores", "Football GPS; force plate (all sports)", "Delivered",
         "Automated pulls twice a day into queryable databases"],
        ["Perch cameras", "Football (Fudge, Simpson, Foster)", "Delivered",
         "Bar-speed tracking live in all three facilities"],
        ["FirstBeat", "Tennis", "Delivered", "Replaced Polar heart-rate monitors"],
        ["Polar straps + Kinexon", "Women's Basketball", "In development",
         "Heart rate paired with Kinexon tracking"],
        ["Analytics platform review", "Department", "In development",
         "Databricks demonstration October 5"],
    ],
    widths=[1.4, 1.75, 1.0, 2.55],
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Section 2
d.section("Department Operations")
d.subhead("2.1  Organizational Structure")
d.para("**Director of Applied Performance: Eric Rash.** Strategic direction, vendor relations, "
       "technology review, research and education. Adjunct instructor, HHPR 5355 (Spring 2026).")
d.para("**Applied Performance Specialist: AJ Tademy.** Football; owned fall camp planning and "
       "the plan-versus-actual review to the football staff in 2026.")
d.para("**Staff development.** Eric leads every-other-week Applied Performance staff meetings "
       "and written development plans for AJ, Noah (Basketball graduate assistant) and Linda "
       "(Tennis and Athletic Performance projects).")
d.para("**Staffing change.** Blake Wright, who carried much of the research work with HHPR, "
       "left mid-year. Research paused as a result and is regaining traction this fall, "
       "starting with the women's health survey data set for Dr. Gallucci.")

d.subhead("2.2  Service Delivery Model")
d.bullets([
    "**Performance testing.** Force plate testing in scheduled lifts for 15 sports, now stored "
    "centrally with automatic updates.",
    "**Training load monitoring.** GPS (Football), Kinexon (Women's Basketball, Volleyball), "
    "heart rate (Tennis, Women's Basketball) and bar speed (Perch).",
    "**Data and reporting.** Sport dashboards and coach reports built on shared stores, so "
    "every report reads from the same numbers.",
    "**Education.** Graduate teaching (HHPR 5355), staff talks, TeamTalk short talks, Research "
    "in 5 paper reviews and the return-to-play course for Athletic Medicine.",
    "**Technology review.** The department-wide inventory and the software cost review with "
    "the Business Office.",
])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Section 3
d.section("Research & Innovation")
d.subhead("3.1  Academic Partnerships: Robbins College, HHPR")
d.para("Work with Dr. Andrew Gallucci's group continued into the fall: a cold-room recovery "
       "study, a DEXA body composition study in planning, and the iron-status manuscript "
       "resubmitted to the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research. The athletics "
       "research steering committee met and approved its first project (a force plate injury "
       "study) on January 30. Research paused after the staff departure; the restart is the "
       "women's health survey data set, cleaned and documented, for Dr. Gallucci by December 11.")
d.para("**S2 Cognition offensive line review.** A planned analysis of 15 offensive linemen "
       "tested whether S2's overall score hides useful differences. The result was null and the "
       "department reported it that way, in a de-identified report.")

d.subhead("3.2  Publications")
d.para("Pickler MC, Gallucci AR, Lee KM, Bolden LK, **Rash ER**, Tinsley GM. Body composition "
       "changes in NCAA Division I female soccer players throughout collegiate playing career. "
       "J Strength Cond Res. 2025 Dec. doi:10.1519/JSC.0000000000005238")
d.para("Applied Performance contributed data: Pickler MC, Funderburk LK, Lee KM, Bolden LK, "
       "Chapman-Lopez TJ, Heileson JL, Gallucci AR. Observation of altered iron status "
       "development during noncompetitive season training in NCAA Division I female acrobatics "
       "and tumbling athletes. J Strength Cond Res. 2026 Jun. doi:10.1519/JSC.0000000000005584")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Section 4
d.section("Unit Goals & Objectives 2026/27")
d.para("The 2026/27 goals are the delivery schedule for what was built this year. Quarters run "
       "with the report year: Q1 October-December 2026, Q2 January-March 2027, Q3 April-June "
       "2027, Q4 July-September 2027.")

d.subhead("Goal 1: Student-Athlete and Staff Education")
d.para("**Objective:** Turn the built library into delivered sessions, each with a named "
       "audience and a date.")
d.table(
    ["Key Result Indicator", "Quarter", "Audience"],
    [
        ["Research in 5 #002 (thoracic outlet) sent; then one review a month", "Q1, then monthly",
         "Athletic Performance staff"],
        ["Intern Curriculum Module 1 delivered", "Q1 (Oct 9)", "Applied Performance interns"],
        ["Applied Performance Playbook Chapter 1 (ForceDecks jump testing) published",
         "Q1 (Oct 23)", "Athletic Performance staff"],
        ["Four TeamTalk pieces delivered, chosen from strength coach interviews", "Q1 (Dec 11)",
         "Student Services leadership; Athletic Performance staff"],
        ["Return-to-play course: six lessons finished; Joe Smith runs one real session",
         "Q1 (Dec 11)", "Joe Smith, Athletic Medicine"],
        ["Performance Academy: sleep, travel and recovery talks in team meetings", "Q2",
         "Volleyball and Women's Basketball athletes"],
        ["HHPR 5355 taught again", "Q2-Q3 (Spring 2027)", "HHPR graduate students"],
        ["Performance School modules 1-2 (Technologies; Planning & Monitoring)", "Q2",
         "Athletic Performance staff"],
        ["Performance School modules 3-4 (Load Prescription; Return to Play)", "Q3",
         "Athletic Performance and Athletic Medicine staff"],
    ],
    widths=[3.6, 1.25, 1.85],
)

d.subhead("Goal 2: Analytics and Planning of Sport-Related Data")
d.para("**Objective:** Keep the new stores current, open them to the people who need them, "
       "and choose an analytics platform on evidence.")
d.table(
    ["Key Result Indicator", "Quarter", "Audience"],
    [
        ["Software cost and use-agreement review completed with the Business Office",
         "Q1", "Kenny Boyd; Erin Boyette"],
        ["Executive Team technology summary", "Q1 (by Nov 30)", "Kenny Boyd; Executive Team"],
        ["Performance data protocol v1 circulated and walked through (integration, storage, "
         "dashboards, interpretation)", "Q1 (Dec 11)", "Chris Ruf; Kenny Boyd"],
        ["Volleyball: drill-level Kinexon export for every practice; weekly report all season",
         "Q1", "Wenger; Ryan McGuyre"],
        ["Analytics platform: one-team proof of concept scoped, plus a second platform costed",
         "Q2", "Kenny Boyd"],
        ["Secure access to the central stores for three user groups", "Q3",
         "Applied Performance; Athletic Performance; Athletic Medicine"],
        ["NCAA best-practice guide for data and technology", "Q3", "Chris Ruf"],
    ],
    widths=[3.6, 1.25, 1.85],

d.para("**Objective:** Restart research with HHPR on existing data, and put one finding into "

d.table(

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.
